title: Mouse Without Borders keyboard destination after using the other device's trackpad

status.label: Test mixed-device input routing
status.detail: Unassigned report with explicit two-device steps; a later tracking overview is not an implementation or ownership claim.

next_action.label: Compare local focus and remote destination
next_action.reason: A local trackpad click may change window focus without switching where the other computer sends keyboard input.

judgment.rationale: The supplied sequence can distinguish stale destination state from intentional independent-input behavior without asking the reporter to gather maintainer traces.
evidence: Reported on 0.83.0 with a desktop keyboard and laptop trackpad: typing works after selecting the laptop textbox using the desktop pointer, but not after using the laptop pointer.
No issue comments or assignees are present.
The timeline links https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/51077, a grouped tracking overview rather than a fix.
Common.DesMachineID delegates to MachineStuff.desMachineID; input routing has explicit machine destination state.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the two-physical-PC input-source matrix and establish intended routing semantics before accepting the proposed synchronization change.

fix_assessment.rationale: A destination-state correction may be applicable, but current evidence does not establish whether the requested any-keyboard behavior is supported.

proposed_fixes.title: Synchronize keyboard routing with accepted local input ownership
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: clicking with the laptop's local trackpad changes foreground focus there but leaves the desktop's shared-input destination unchanged; this may instead reflect intentional input ownership semantics.
plan: Trace Common.DesMachineID and MachineStuff switching alongside InputHook callbacks for both physical input sources, using src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Core/Common.cs and Core/MachineStuff.cs.
Agree whether accepted local physical input should transfer shared keyboard ownership; do not implement cross-device last-focus behavior without this contract decision.

If transfer is intended, update destination through the existing machine-switch protocol on local ownership acquisition, excluding injected events and guarding against loops or broadcast-mode regressions.
Add two-machine routing tests for local/remote clicks, disconnected peers and simultaneous input.
verification: On two physical computers, execute the original four steps with a harmless textbox on each and record where desktop keystrokes arrive.
Compare with desktop-pointer selection, explicit machine switching and simultaneous local typing; ensure no keystrokes are duplicated or routed to an unintended machine.

confidence.rationale: Explicit destination state supports the hypothesis, but no runtime trace or supported-semantics decision identifies a confirmed defect.

issue_context.summary: A laptop trackpad can focus a textbox on the laptop, but the desktop keyboard cannot type there until the desktop pointer selects that textbox.
known_information: The report supplies two machines, distinct keyboard/pointer sources, and a working desktop-pointer workaround.
Reported on 0.83.0; live issue remains open and unassigned.
Tracking overview #51077 includes this report; no matching fix PR was found.
inferences: Window focus on one computer and the other computer's remote-input destination may be independent.
issue_context.analysis: Do not equate a focused textbox with confirmed remote keyboard ownership. The discriminating work is a maintainer-side input-source experiment, not a generic log request.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full report, empty discussion, cross-reference timeline and related PR search.
Inspected Common.DesMachineID, MachineStuff destination fields and InputHook keyboard/mouse entry points in the upstream MouseWithoutBorders source.

actions.label: Test desktop keyboard after laptop trackpad focus

prerequisites: Two physical PCs: desktop keyboard/mouse and laptop with trackpad; paired and connected.
Open a harmless text editor on each; record input-sharing settings.
steps: Using the laptop trackpad, select a textbox on the desktop.
Using that trackpad, select a textbox on the laptop.
Type a distinctive harmless string using the desktop keyboard and record its actual destination.
Select the laptop textbox using the desktop mouse, type again, and compare destination state on both computers.
Repeat using explicit machine switching and trace physical versus injected input.
reproduce.expected_result: Characterize whether the shared destination follows the last local click; if that is the supported contract, desktop typing must reach the laptop exactly once.

actions.label: Approve input-ownership investigation plan
actions.note: Low-confidence conditional fix; settle input-ownership semantics and reproduce before changing routing.
